dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you think Nacker stole the core?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Do you still remember when I was flipping through the pictures Ms. Chronie took in the ruins?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: There's one of Nacker working in front of the suppression device. It's quite blurry... but I'm quite certain that his actions are definitely not part of any operational procedure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That doesn't really mean anything, though. Maybe... maybe a thief came flying across from the nearby mountain and stole the core?

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Heh, that's most definitely impossible. The energy flow of the Arkhium in the ruins is the best anti-theft measure there is. No ordinary person can withstand it.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Besides, the timing of the Experimental Field Generator's activation is simply too perfect. It cannot be a mere coincidence...

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I have a preliminary conjecture. Nacker — or should I say, the one who stole the core — likely removed the Arkhium Kinetic Core early on, activating the backup energy source.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: However, Pneumousia Cores are relatively inefficient energy sources, and they have to keep up a continuous output of energy to reach the activation threshold of this contraption here.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Hence, this person intentionally activated that large Arkhium chunk, creating a modest, but rather noticeable explosion.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: This way, when the Institute sent someone to investigate, they would be certain to fix the Arkhium Inhibitor first.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: And by the time they realized that they'd have to go to the Experimental Field Generator to retrieve the backup energy supply, the Generator would have already finished charging.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: From a technical perspective, such a modus operandi is highly probable, and those within the Institute capable of doing this would only be Edwin, Mr. Nacker, and myself.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: I doubt Edwin had the opportunity to do anything to that effect... which leaves two remaining suspects. Myself, and Mr. Nacker.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe this was all your doing, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! You said that Nacker lied, but you've also been lying all along!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe this was all just part of your plan, and you tricked us into escorting you here so you could grab whatever it was you wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Your accusation is not entirely baseless. After this, I will also apply for and submit myself to the Institute's credibility review.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: As far as I'm concerned, though, Mr. Nacker is the one more likely to have committed this act. If this really was his doing, then he should be the one with the most to gain from it.

dialogues.speaker: Raimondo
dialogues.text: Even if I am listed alongside him as a suspect... his chances of being convicted are certainly greater than mine.
